breakfast.name: Fry Jacks
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt
Cut in shortening, add water to form dough
Rest 10 min, roll thin, cut triangles
Deep fry until puffed and golden
Serve with beans, cheese, or jam
breakfast.description: Puffy fried dough triangles — the Belizean breakfast staple.

breakfast.name: Johnny Cakes with Refried Beans
instructions: Make dough with flour, baking powder, coconut oil, milk
Shape rounds, bake at 200°C 20 min
Mash cooked beans, fry with onion, garlic, cumin
Serve johnny cakes split open with refried beans
breakfast.description: Coconut-scented biscuits with creamy refried beans.

breakfast.name: Fry Jacks
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt
Cut in shortening
Add water to form soft dough, rest 15 min
Divide into balls, roll into oval shapes
Cut each oval in half diagonally
Deep fry until puffed and golden
Serve with refried beans, cheese, or jam
breakfast.description: Puffy fried dough triangles — THE Belizean breakfast. Crispy outside, airy inside, always with beans and cheese.

lunch.name: Rice and Beans with Stew Chicken
instructions: Season chicken with recado rojo, garlic, cumin
Brown chicken, add onion, thyme, habanero, water
Simmer 30 min
Cook rice with beans and coconut milk
Serve stew chicken over coconut rice and beans
lunch.description: Belizean comfort food — coconut rice and beans topped with stew chicken.

lunch.name: Garnaches
instructions: Fry tortillas until crisp
Spread with refried beans
Top with grated cheese
Add pickled onion and hot sauce
lunch.description: Crispy tortillas topped with beans, cheese, and pickled onion.

lunch.name: Garnaches
instructions: Fry tortillas until crispy
Spread thick layer of refried beans
Top with shredded cabbage, crumbled cheese, pickled onion
Drizzle habanero sauce
lunch.description: Crispy tortillas loaded with beans and toppings — Belizean street food found at every market stall.

dinner.name: Hudut (Fish Coconut Stew)
instructions: Boil and mash plantains into thick fudoo
Simmer fish in coconut milk with onion, garlic, thyme, habanero
Cook until fish is flaky and sauce thickens
Squeeze lime juice in
Serve coconut fish stew over mashed plantain
dinner.description: Garifuna coconut fish stew served over mashed plantain.

dinner.name: Tamales (Belizean Style)
ingredients: Masa: 4 cups masa harina, 1 cup lard, chicken broth
Filling: 500g chicken, recado rojo, 2 tomatoes, 1 onion, olives, capers
instructions: Make masa with lard and broth until smooth
Cook chicken with recado rojo, tomatoes, onion
Shred chicken, add olives and capers
Spread masa on plantain leaf, add filling
Wrap tightly, tie with string
Steam 90 min
dinner.description: Masa packets steamed in plantain leaves, a Belizean celebration food.

dinner.name: Boil Up (Creole One-Pot)
instructions: Boil pig tail until tender
Add hard root vegetables: cassava, sweet potato, cocoyam
Cook 15 min, add green plantain
Add ripe plantain last (it cooks fast)
Season broth with onion, tomato sauce, habanero
Cook until everything is tender but not falling apart
Serve with broth ladled over
dinner.description: Creole boil-up — salted meat simmered with every root vegetable in Belize. Saturday lunch tradition.

snacks.name: Panades (Fried Stuffed Tortillas)
ingredients: Filling: 300g shark or other fish, 1 onion, recado rojo, vinegar, habanero
instructions: Make masa dough
Cook fish with recado rojo and onion, flake
Shape masa into cups, fill with fish
Seal and flatten slightly
Deep fry until crispy
Serve with pickled onion and habanero sauce
snacks.description: Crispy fried masa pockets stuffed with seasoned fish.

snacks.name: Panades (Fried Corn Pockets)
instructions: Season fish with recado rojo, onion, habanero
Shape corn masa into thick discs
Fill with fish, fold into half-moon
Seal edges tightly
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve with pickled onion and habanero salsa
snacks.description: Crispy fried corn pockets stuffed with seasoned fish — a Maya-Mestizo snack sold fresh from roadside stalls.

snacks.name: Fry Jacks
ingredients: Warm water (enough to make soft dough)
Refried beans, cheese, or jam for filling
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, salt
Cut in shortening
Add warm water gradually until soft, not sticky dough forms
Knead briefly, rest 10 min
Roll out and cut into triangles
Deep fry in hot oil — they puff up dramatically into pillows
Drain on paper
Split open and fill with refried beans and cheese, or butter and jam for sweet version
Every Belizean morning starts with these — the puff-up moment is the viral hook
snacks.description: Belize's breakfast staple — fried dough triangles that puff up into golden pillows. Split and stuffed with beans and cheese or jam. The dramatic puffing moment went viral, and fry jacks are now the most recognized Belizean food worldwide.

desserts.name: Tres Leches Cake
ingredients: For cake: 5 eggs, 1 cup sugar, 1.5 cups flour, baking powder, vanilla
Three milks: 1 can condensed milk, 1 can evaporated milk, 1 cup heavy cream
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar until fluffy, fold in flour
Bake at 175°C 30 min
Cool, poke holes all over
Mix three milks, pour over cake slowly
Refrigerate overnight
Top with whipped cream and cinnamon
desserts.description: Sponge cake soaked in three milks — incredibly moist.

desserts.name: Sweet Potato Pone
instructions: Mix grated sweet potato with coconut milk, sugar, spices
Add melted butter and raisins
Pour into greased baking dish
Bake at 175°C for 40-45 min until set and browned on top
Cool before slicing — it firms as it cools
desserts.description: Dense, spiced sweet potato pudding — Belizean comfort dessert with Creole roots.

drinks.name: Seaweed Shake
instructions: Boil seaweed until dissolved
Strain, blend with milk, condensed milk, vanilla, spices
Serve cold over ice
drinks.description: A thick, creamy seaweed-based milkshake — a Belizean classic.

drinks.name: Cashew Wine
instructions: Wash and crush cashew fruit
Boil in water 20 min, strain
Add sugar, cool to room temp
Add yeast, ferment 7-10 days
Strain and bottle
drinks.description: Homemade wine from the cashew fruit.

imageCredit.author: Simon Law from Montréal, QC, Canada

drinks.name: Seaweed Drink
instructions: Soak seaweed overnight, rinse well
Boil with cinnamon stick until it dissolves into gel
Strain, blend with milks, nutmeg, vanilla
Sweeten to taste
Serve cold over ice
drinks.description: Thick, creamy seaweed drink — an island specialty believed to be a natural energy booster. Popular across the cayes.
